transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm in the right place. It's probably nothing too major, really, just a little hiccup with my workflow lately. 

What finally pushed me to make this appointment is... well, I keep starting follow-up items after my audits, or after mentorship events at work, and I have every intention of finishing them right then and there. But then, I don't know, I guess I get a little sidetracked? And I'll find out days later that the final email, or the review note, or the form... it never actually got done. Which isn't like me, usually! I try to be very reliable. Is that... does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right.
How much distress or worry have these unfinished tasks been causing you?

Well, I try not to make a fuss about things, but... I guess it has been causing me a fair bit of worry. I just really hate letting people down, you know? 

Like, at work, it kind of reached a point recently where... um... well, a client review was actually affected because of an unfinished follow-up. We got it sorted out! But I've been so anxious that management might be questioning whether I can handle this promotion I'm up for. I really don't want them to think I'm careless, because I'm normally not. 

And, um... it's a little embarrassing to admit this part, but at home, my husband has actually had to take over paying the bills and a few other commitments I originally agreed to do. He's been very patient about it, but it's mostly because he feels he can't really count on me to complete them reliably right now. Which makes me feel awful, honestly. I should be able to handle these basic things, right? I just hope I'm not overreacting or making too big a deal out of all this... does it sound like I'm overthinking it?
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless when you're supposed to be sitting still?

Well, I guess... maybe a little bit? I mean, I try very hard to be professional, especially during long audits or board meetings. But, um, I suppose I do have a habit of... well, keeping my hands or feet busy. 

Like, when I'm sitting in meetings, I'm usually tapping my foot under the table, or maybe clicking my pen a little. Just small things! I try to keep it very quiet so it doesn't bother anyone. Though, I will admit, I tend to shift around in my chair a fair amount. My colleague actually joked the other day that she can hear my leg going under the desk. I was so embarrassed! I really hope it doesn't make me look unprofessional or like I'm not paying attention, because I really am trying to listen. Is that... is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope that's an okay answer.
Do you often have difficulty paying attention to details or making careless mistakes in your work or other activities?

Oh... gosh. Um... I really try my best to be perfectly accurate. I mean, in my line of work, detail is supposed to be my main strength, right? So it's a little hard to admit this, but... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, there have been a few slip-ups lately. Nothing intentional, I promise! 

But, um, in reports that I absolutely know better than to rush through, I'll sometimes... well, I might miss a changed date, or accidentally transpose a number. Once or twice I've even left a placeholder comment in the workpaper by mistake. It's just incredibly embarrassing when it happens, because I really do pride myself on my work. I always try to catch it and fix it right away! I hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent... I really do care about doing things right and being thorough. Does that answer your question okay?
Do you often act on impulse without fully thinking things through?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I really try my best to be very careful before making any decisions. I mean, being an accountant, you kind of have to weigh everything out and follow the rules, right? So I don't really just jump into things without thinking them through. 

I would just hate to make a mess of things for anyone else by being reckless. I mean, maybe everyone has a tiny moment here and there, like, I don't know, buying a coffee I didn't plan on, but nothing major, I promise! I always try to be very responsible about my choices so I don't cause any problems. Is that... does that answer what you were looking for? I hope I'm understanding the question right.
When did you first notice these changes in your ability to complete tasks and pay attention to details?

Oh, um... well, it hasn't always been this much of a struggle, I promise. I've always been very capable and organized. But, um... I guess I'd say it's been a bit harder for about... maybe a year and 10 months? Give or take? 

It actually started right after I got a promotion. Which was wonderful, really! I had just won this firm-wide award, and they moved me up, which I was so grateful for. But, um, with the promotion came a lot more responsibilities and a much heavier workload. I think... well, I think just trying to juggle all the new expectations made it a little trickier for me to keep all the plates spinning, so to speak. I really am trying my absolute hardest to stay on top of everything, though! I just... I hope that doesn't make it sound like I can't handle my job. Is that the sort of timeline you were wondering about?
Have you noticed any changes in your relationships with friends or family members since you started having trouble completing tasks and paying attention to details?

Oh, um... relationships? Well, I mean, everyone has been so incredibly supportive, really. My husband is just wonderful. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, things have been a little... strained? Just a tiny bit. 

I feel terrible about it, but... well, at home, I was sort of letting a few things slip through the cracks. Just little things, like paying a bill on time or remembering a dinner we'd RSVP'd to. So my husband has actually had to take over managing the bills and our social calendar. I feel so guilty because I promised I would handle them, but he just... well, he said he couldn't quite count on me to get them done right now. I'm really trying to get back on track so he doesn't have to carry that burden, I promise.

And, um, at work... well, it's a little embarrassing to admit. I try so hard to be perfect for my clients, but some of those slip-ups I mentioned earlier... they actually affected a client review recently. Nothing catastrophic! But enough that... well, I worry my colleagues might be starting to question if I was really the right choice for that promotion. I just hate the idea of letting anyone down or making them regret believing in me. 

Does that... I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible wife or employee. I really do care so much about the people around me. Is that what you were asking about?
Have you had to cut back on any work or social activities because of your difficulty with completing tasks or paying attention to details?

Oh, um... cut back on activities? Well, I wouldn't say I've completely stopped doing things, I really try to keep up! But, um... I guess I have had to step back just a little bit. 

Like I mentioned before, at home, my husband has taken over the bills and our social calendar. I feel just awful about it, but he said he couldn't quite count on me to complete them reliably right now. So I guess I have cut back on managing those commitments, even though I agreed to them. I'm really hoping to take them back soon so he doesn't have to do all that extra work!

And at work... well, I haven't officially cut back my hours or anything, but because of those mistakes and the unfinished follow-ups that affected the client review... I've sort of been stepping back from taking the lead on things. I just worry so much that people are questioning whether I can actually handle the promotion, and I'd hate to make any more errors that cause problems for the firm. So I guess I have been a little less involved than I was right after I got promoted. 

I hope that makes sense? I really am trying my best to fix it, I promise I'm not just giving up on my responsibilities! Does that answer your question?
Do you often feel like you're constantly on the go, even when you're not necessarily supposed to be doing something active?

Oh, um... constantly on the go? Well, I mean, I like to stay productive! It's important to me to contribute, you know? But... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest, maybe I do have a little trouble just... sitting still. 

Like on the weekends, I always tell my husband, "Okay, this weekend I am just going to rest and recharge." I really mean it when I say it! But then... well, I'll start a load of laundry, and while that's running, I'll think, "Oh, I should just check my work email real quick," and then suddenly I'm out the door for a run, and when I get back I'm trying to organize things for my volunteer committee... and before I know it, I've just sort of bounced from one thing to the next all day long. I don't really stop until I'm just completely exhausted. 

I just... I like to be helpful, and I hate feeling like I'm wasting time. I hope that doesn't make me sound frantic or, you know, incapable of relaxing. I just have a lot of energy, I guess! Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your overall quality of life since you started experiencing these difficulties with task completion and attention to detail?

Oh, um... quality of life? Well, I mean, I still have a wonderful life, really! I have so much to be thankful for, and I don't want to sound like I'm complaining at all. But... I suppose, if I'm being totally honest, the things I mentioned earlier have made things feel a little... heavy lately?

Like at work... just knowing that my mistakes and those unfinished follow-ups actually reached the point of affecting a client review... it just sort of hangs over me. I go into the office and I have this little knot in my stomach, worrying that everyone is questioning whether I can actually handle that promotion. I just hate the idea that I'm letting the firm down, you know? 

And then at home... well, like I said, my husband having to take over the bills and those commitments I agreed to, just because he can't count on me to complete them reliably right now... it really takes a toll on how I feel about myself. I want to be a good partner, and it makes me feel so terribly guilty to put that extra weight on him. 

So I guess, overall, it has caused a bit of a strain on my day-to-day happiness and my confidence. But I'm really determined to work through it and get back to being my best self! Does that... does that answer what you were asking? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Did you have any difficulties with paying attention or completing tasks when you were a child?

Oh, um... as a child? Well, I actually always tried really hard in school! I really wanted to be a good student and please my teachers. But... I suppose, if I'm looking back at elementary school, there were a few little hiccups. 

My report cards usually said I was bright, which was always so nice to hear! But they also... well, my teachers would often write that I lost my assignments, or that I sort of rushed past the small details. And I guess I did talk out of turn sometimes—I think I was just always so eager to participate, you know? But I did need a few extra reminders to actually finish my work once I started it. 

My mother actually still jokes about it today. She always says that I could completely ace a test, but then I'd completely forget to turn in the big project that was just sitting right there at the bottom of my backpack. It's sort of a funny family story now, but I always felt a little bad about making her worry. 

I really did try my best, though! I hope that's the kind of thing you were asking about? Am I giving you the right information?
Did you have any difficulties with paying attention or completing tasks consistently throughout your childhood and adolescence?

Oh, um... throughout my whole childhood and adolescence? Well... like I said, I did have those little hiccups when I was younger, but I always managed to get by okay! I really tried hard to keep things together, and I did fine through high school and college. 

Actually, the things we've been talking about—the trouble at work and everything—it hasn't really been a lifelong struggle like this. It's really only been... well, noticeably difficult for maybe the last year and ten months or so? 

I had actually won a firm-wide award, which was such an honor, and right after that they gave me a promotion. I was so thrilled! But... with the promotion came a lot more responsibilities and a much heavier workload. I think that's when I really started to find it all just... much harder to juggle. I just wanted to do a good job in the new role, but it's been a bit overwhelming since then. 

I hope it's okay that this is a more recent change? I know you asked about my childhood, but I just want to make sure I'm giving you the most accurate picture of when things really started to feel like a problem. Does that make sense?
Have you ever been diagnosed with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder or does your family have a history of it?

Oh, um... diagnosed? No, no, I've never been diagnosed with anything like that. I've always just thought of myself as someone who maybe needs to try a little harder to stay organized, you know? 

And as for my family... well, we don't really talk about things like that very much. Everyone in my family is just so hardworking and successful. I suppose my brother has always been a little... well, a little energetic, maybe? He tends to jump from project to project, but he's a wonderful person, very creative! But no, nobody has ever had an official diagnosis or anything. 

I hope that's helpful? I just wouldn't want to make it sound like there's some big family history when there isn't. Is that the kind of background information you need?
Did you experience significant difficulties with paying attention or completing tasks during most of your childhood?

Oh, um... I hope I'm not repeating myself too much! I think... well, like I mentioned just a little bit earlier, I really wouldn't call them *significant* difficulties. I don't want to make it sound worse than it was, because I really did try so hard to be a good student! 

But yes, um, even back in elementary school, my report cards did have those little notes. They always said I was bright—which was very kind of them!—but they also mentioned that I lost assignments, or rushed past the small details, and maybe talked out of turn a bit. And I definitely needed some reminders to actually finish my work once I started it. 

And, just like I was saying before, my mother still jokes about how I could completely ace a test but then forget the big project that was sitting right there in my backpack. 

I hope it's okay that I brought that up again? I know we just touched on it, I just want to make sure I'm answering you properly and giving you exactly what you need! Am I on the right track?
Did your difficulties with paying attention and completing tasks cause significant problems for you in social or occupational settings before the age of 12?

Oh, um... before I was 12? No, no, I wouldn't say they caused *significant* problems at all. I mean, obviously I didn't have a job back then, but as far as school and friends went... everything was mostly fine! 

Like I mentioned, I did have those little notes on my report cards about rushing or talking, but I never got into any real trouble, and I got along really well with the other kids and my teachers. I was always very eager to help out in class, actually! I really don't want to give you the impression that I was a difficult child or a bad student, because I always tried my absolute best to be good and do what was asked of me. 

So, no, nothing I would call a significant problem back then. I hope that makes sense? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right kind of information!
Have you experienced difficulties with task completion or attention to detail in settings outside of work, such as in hobbies or volunteering?

Oh, um... well, I suppose... yes, a little bit? I mean, I really try my best to keep everything running smoothly, but... well, at home, my husband is just so wonderful and supportive. I get so overwhelmed sometimes, and I think he realized he couldn't always count on me to get them done on time. I feel terrible about it, really, because I don't want to be a burden to him!

I'm an accountant, and lately... well, I've made a few little mistakes. And some follow-ups haven't been finished quite when they should have been. I don't want to sound like I'm failing at everything, because I really do work so hard! I just... I hope I'm not oversharing or making it sound worse than it is. Is that the kind of information you were looking for?
Did you experience any difficulties with paying attention or completing tasks before the age of 7?

Oh, um... before I was 7? I really don't think so. I mean, that's so little, isn't it? Just kindergarten and first grade, mostly. 

I honestly don't remember having any real trouble back then. I think I was just a normal, happy little girl! I loved playing and coloring, and I don't recall my parents or teachers ever being worried about me paying attention when I was that young. I was always very eager to please the grown-ups, even back then. 

I really hope that's helpful! I know my memory from that far back might not be perfect, but I'm trying my absolute best to give you the right answers. Am I doing okay?
Have you experienced difficulties with task completion or attention to detail in multiple areas of your life, such as at work, at home, or in your free time?

Oh, um... well, I guess since we just talked about home and work, it does seem like it's happening in a couple of places, doesn't it? I really hate to admit it, because I don't want you to think I'm completely falling apart or anything! 

But, yes, I suppose it is in both areas. Like I was saying, at work, those little mistakes and the unfinished follow-ups... they really did affect that client review. And I'm just so worried that people are starting to doubt if I'm ready for that promotion. I try so hard to be perfect, but it just slips through the cracks sometimes. 

And then at home, with my husband having to take over the bills and the things I promised I'd handle... it's just because he can't rely on me to get them done when I'm supposed to. I feel awful that it's bleeding into my marriage and my job. I really want to be dependable in both places, I promise I do! 

Does that answer your question? I know I'm sort of repeating myself from a minute ago, I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know.

Oh, my entire life? No, no, definitely not! I really don't want you to think I've always been disorganized or struggling like this. I've actually always prided myself on working very, very hard to keep everything together!

Have you experienced significant difficulties with attention or task completion for more than 6 months?

Oh, yes, definitely more than six months. Like I mentioned a moment ago, it's been about... well, a year and ten months now. 

I really try to keep track of these things because I want to give you accurate information! But yes, it started right around the time I got that promotion. Winning that firm-wide award was such an honor, and I was so, so thrilled... but then the new workload hit. I just... I really want to do a good job, and I've been trying so hard to keep up with the extra responsibilities, but it's just been so much harder to juggle everything since then.
